title: Yesterday's bento
setting: Sunday lunchtime at Kenta and Sora's flat. Last night Kenta made hot pot for Yuki and Mai. Mai drops by to pick up the glasses she left behind, just as Sora, barely awake, is about to heat up a bento he bought yesterday.

speakers.name: Mai
speakers.voice: female, late 20s, warm, a little shy

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: sora, kinou nando mo renraku shita n da yo.
lines.ja: ソラ、昨日何度も連絡したんだよ。
lines.kana: そら、きのうなんどもれんらくしたんだよ。
lines.english: Sora, I messaged you loads of times last night.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: gomen, juuden kireteta. dou shita no?
lines.ja: ごめん、充電切れてた。どうしたの？
lines.kana: ごめん、じゅうでんきれてた。どうしたの？
lines.english: Sorry, my battery was dead. What's up?

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: megane, koko ni nai? kinou, nabe no toki hazushite, wasurechatta.
lines.ja: メガネ、ここにない？昨日、鍋のとき外して、忘れちゃった。
lines.kana: めがね、ここにない？きのう、なべのときはずして、わすれちゃった。
lines.english: Are my glasses here? I took them off while we were having hot pot and left them behind.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: aa, are mai no ka. hora, kore.
lines.ja: ああ、あれマイのか。ほら、これ。
lines.kana: ああ、あれまいのか。ほら、これ。
lines.english: Oh, so those were yours. Here you go.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: yokatta, arigatou. are, ima kara ohiru?
lines.ja: よかった、ありがとう。あれ、今からお昼？
lines.kana: よかった、ありがとう。あれ、いまからおひる？
lines.english: Phew, thanks. Oh, are you just having lunch?

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: un. kinou katta obentou, renji de atatameru tokoro.
lines.ja: うん。昨日買ったお弁当、レンジで温めるところ。
lines.kana: うん。きのうかったおべんとう、れんじであたためるところ。
lines.english: Yeah. I'm about to microwave the bento I bought yesterday.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.ja: 昨日？それ、冷蔵庫に入れた？
lines.kana: きのう？それ、れいぞうこにいれた？
lines.english: Yesterday? Did you put it in the fridge?

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: uun, zutto koko ni atta. nabe tabete, wasureteta.
lines.ja: ううん、ずっとここにあった。鍋食べて、忘れてた。
lines.kana: ううん、ずっとここにあった。なべたべて、わすれてた。
lines.english: Nope, it's been sitting here the whole time. We had hot pot and I forgot all about it.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: a, kore, kigen kireteru yo. kinou no yoru juuji made.
lines.ja: あ、これ、期限切れてるよ。昨日の夜十時まで。
lines.kana: あ、これ、きげんきれてるよ。きのうのよるじゅうじまで。
lines.english: Oh, this is past its date. It was only good till ten last night.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: demo, kigen chotto kireta dake desho? obentou wa atatamereba daijoubu da yo.
lines.ja: でも、期限ちょっと切れただけでしょ？お弁当は温めれば大丈夫だよ。
lines.kana: でも、きげんちょっときれただけでしょ？おべんとうはあたためればだいじょうぶだよ。
lines.english: But it's only just past, right? A bento's fine if you heat it up.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: dame da yo. reizouko ni iretenakatta shi, kigen mo kireteru n da kara.
lines.ja: だめだよ。冷蔵庫に入れてなかったし、期限も切れてるんだから。
lines.kana: だめだよ。れいぞうこにいれてなかったし、きげんもきれてるんだから。
lines.english: No way. It wasn't in the fridge, and it's past its date as well.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: aa, obentou atatamete taberu tsumori datta noni.
lines.ja: ああ、お弁当温めて食べるつもりだったのに。
lines.kana: ああ、おべんとうあたためてたべるつもりだったのに。
lines.english: Aw, and I was going to heat it up and have it for lunch.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: kinou no nabe, mada aru n ja nai?
lines.ja: 昨日の鍋、まだあるんじゃない？
lines.kana: きのうのなべ、まだあるんじゃない？
lines.english: Isn't there still some hot pot left from last night?

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: a, sou da. kenta ga futa shite, reizouko ni iretoite kureta n da.
lines.ja: あ、そうだ。ケンタが蓋して、冷蔵庫に入れといてくれたんだ。
lines.kana: あ、そうだ。けんたがふたして、れいぞうこにいれといてくれたんだ。
lines.english: Oh, right. Kenta put the lid on and stuck it in the fridge for us.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: honto da, mada ippai aru. sasuga kenta.
lines.ja: ほんとだ、まだいっぱいある。さすがケンタ。
lines.kana: ほんとだ、まだいっぱいある。さすがけんた。
lines.english: So there is, and loads of it. Good old Kenta.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: jaa, futa shite, gofun gurai atatameyou.
lines.ja: じゃあ、蓋して、五分ぐらい温めよう。
lines.kana: じゃあ、ふたして、ごふんぐらいあたためよう。
lines.english: Right, lid on, and we'll heat it for about five minutes.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: un. kondo kara, obentou wa sugu reizouko ni iretoite ne.
lines.ja: うん。今度から、お弁当はすぐ冷蔵庫に入れといてね。
lines.kana: うん。こんどから、おべんとうはすぐれいぞうこにいれといてね。
lines.english: OK. And from now on, put your bento straight in the fridge, alright?

questions.ja: ソラのお昼は、どうなりましたか？
questions.kana: そらのおひるは、どうなりましたか？
questions.romaji: sora no ohiru wa, dou narimashita ka?

choices.english: The microwave wasn't working, so they heated his bento up in a pot instead.
His bento had been left out all night and was past its date, so they heated up the leftover hot pot instead.
Kenta had already finished the leftover hot pot, so Sora heated up his bento after all.

questions.explanation: Sora bought the bento yesterday and it sat out all night (lines 6-8). Mai finds its date ran out at ten last night (line 9) and won't let him eat it, even heated (lines 10-11). So they heat up the hot pot Kenta put in the fridge (lines 13-16). A is wrong: the microwave is never a problem, the bento itself is. C is wrong: the hot pot is still there, and plenty of it (line 15).

questions.english: Sora came over for hot pot at your place, and there's a lot left. He asks, "nabe, mada ippai aru ne. dou suru?" Say you'll put it in the fridge, using reizouko ni ireru.
questions.ja: 鍋、まだいっぱいあるね。どうする？
questions.kana: なべ、まだいっぱいあるね。どうする？
questions.romaji: nabe, mada ippai aru ne. dou suru?
questions.answer: Say it goes in the fridge: reizouko ni ireru, with ni for where the food goes. With -toku it means putting it in there for later: reizouko ni iretoku ne (I'll put it in the fridge).

modelAnswers.ja: じゃあ、冷蔵庫に入れとくね。
modelAnswers.english: I'll put it in the fridge, then.

modelAnswers.romaji: futa shite, reizouko ni irete okou. ashita mo taberareru shi.
modelAnswers.ja: 蓋して、冷蔵庫に入れておこう。明日も食べられるし。
modelAnswers.english: Let's put the lid on and put it in the fridge. We can have it tomorrow too.

questions.explanation: Mai asks 'reizouko ni ireta?' (did you put it in the fridge?) in line 7, Sora says Kenta 'reizouko ni iretoite kureta' (put it in the fridge for us) in line 14, and Mai ends with 'reizouko ni iretoite ne' in line 17. The verb is ireru, put inside; oku, the English 'put', is setting something down on a surface. Keep ni: it marks where the food goes, unlike satou o ireru, where o marks what goes in.

questions.english: Mai tells Sora his bento is past its date. What does Sora say about it?
questions.ja: ソラは、お弁当について何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: そらは、おべんとうについてなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: sora wa, obentou ni tsuite nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: It would be fine if he put it in the fridge for a while first.
It tastes fine cold, so there's no need to heat it.
It would be fine to eat as long as he heated it up.

questions.explanation: Line 10: 'obentou wa atatamereba daijoubu da yo' (a bento's fine if you heat it up). atatameru is heating food up, and -ba makes it 'if you heat it'. A is wrong: he says nothing about the fridge, and the bento had never been in it, which is Mai's point in line 11. B is wrong: he wants it hot. In line 6 he was about to heat it in the microwave ('renji de atatameru tokoro'), and in line 12 he says he'd planned to heat it up and eat it.

questions.english: There's still plenty of hot pot left. What does Sora say as they heat it up?
questions.ja: 鍋を温めるとき、ソラは何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: なべをあたためるとき、そらはなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: nabe o atatameru toki, sora wa nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: lid on, and heat it for about five minutes
choices.romaji: jaa, futa shite, gofun gurai atatameyou.

choices.english: set the lid down, and heat it for about five minutes
choices.romaji: jaa, futa oite, gofun gurai atatameyou.

choices.english: lid off, and heat it for about five minutes
choices.romaji: jaa, futa totte, gofun gurai atatameyou.

questions.explanation: Line 16: 'futa shite' (put the lid on). A lid goes on with suru, the same suru as masuku o suru, and Kenta did the same before the pot went in the fridge (line 14: 'futa shite, reizouko ni iretoite kureta'). B is the English 'put the lid on' turned word for word into futa o oku, which means setting the lid down somewhere, so the pot would heat uncovered. C, futa o toru, takes the lid off: the opposite of what Sora does after Mai has looked inside.

questions.english: Sora offers you a bento from yesterday. You check the label: its date ran out last night. He asks, "kore, kinou no obentou da kedo, taberu?" Tell him it's past its date, using kigen ga kireru.
questions.ja: これ、昨日のお弁当だけど、食べる？
questions.kana: これ、きのうのおべんとうだけど、たべる？
questions.romaji: kore, kinou no obentou da kedo, taberu?
questions.answer: Say it's past its date: kigen kireteru (ga often drops in casual talk), with kireru, the verb for something running out. Then turn it down.

modelAnswers.ja: ううん、それ期限切れてるよ。

modelAnswers.romaji: a, kigen ga kireteru kara, yametoku.
modelAnswers.ja: あ、期限が切れてるから、やめとく。
modelAnswers.english: Oh, it's past its date, so I'll pass.

questions.explanation: Mai says 'kigen kireteru yo' in line 9 and 'kigen mo kireteru' in line 11, and Sora's 'kigen chotto kireta dake desho?' in line 10 is the past form. 'Expire' needs no special verb: a date runs out with kireru, just as Sora's phone battery did in line 2 ('juuden kireteta'). Don't mix it up with kigen ga warui, 'in a bad mood', which is a different kigen.
